newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Central Bank archives to open to Nazi probe.
newsitem.headline: Central Bank archives to open to Nazi probe.

text.p: President Carlos Menem on Monday ordered the Central Bank archives be opened to help investigate whether Nazi funds were deposited in Argentina during the Second World War, Interior Minister Carlos Corach said.
At the request of international Jewish organizations, Menem "ordered the total opening of the Central Bank archives ... to check a list of 334 persons," Corach told journalists.
He did not identify the owners of those accounts.

Jewish organizations have been trying to trace gold looted by the Nazis and some of them suspect that what went to Latin America landed in Argentina, although from there it may have passed to other countries like Chile.

Newly discovered U.S. documents that were revealed in January showed that at the height of the war the Swiss National Bank sent 280 truckloads of looted Nazi gold to Spain and Portugal in vehicles bearing neutral Switzerland's national emblem.

Jewish groups requested that Switzerland investigate all secret bank accounts of Nazi officials and the money be given to the victims of the Holocaust. They are also investigating a golden triangle between Germany, Spain and Argentina.
Corach said the Jewish groups' request was aimed at "banking accounts that could exist in Argentina, connected to funds deviated during World War II and immediately afterwards."
Once the information is gathered, the Argentine government will send it to the requesting organizations, he added, without identifying them.
